questions.questionText: A tank is filled by pipes A and B together in some time. If pipe B (which alone takes 15 hours) is replaced by pipe C (which alone takes 6 hours), by how much does the filling time change? Pipe A alone takes 10 hours.

questions.explanationText: Time for X = 2000/25 = 80 minutes and time for Y = 3000/25 = 120 minutes. Difference = 40 minutes.

questions.questionText: A pump delivers 30 litres per minute. It fills tank X of capacity 1500 litres and then tank Y of capacity 4500 litres. How much longer does tank Y take than tank X?

questions.questionText: The times taken by pipes A and B to fill a tank separately are in the ratio 2 : 5. If pipe A alone takes 12 hours, how long will both pipes together take?

questions.questionText: The times taken by pipes A and B to fill a tank separately are in the ratio 4 : 7. If pipe A alone takes 20 hours, how long will both pipes together take?

questions.questionText: The times taken by pipes A and B to fill a tank separately are in the ratio 1 : 2. If pipe A alone takes 9 hours, how long will both pipes together take?

questions.questionText: A pipe pours water into a tank of capacity 900 litres at 45 litres per minute, but a leak at the bottom makes the tank take 15 minutes to fill. At what rate does the leak drain water?
questions.explanationText: Effective filling rate = 900 ÷ 15 = 60 litres per minute. Leak rate = 45 - 60 = -15 litres per minute.

questions.questionText: Two inlet pipes alone fill a tank in 10 hours and 15 hours. With an outlet pipe also open, the tank fills in 12 hours. How long will the outlet pipe alone take to empty the full tank?
